title: Vendor governance, integrations, and SLA acceptance preflight
next_steps: Alex to send redwood security pack + SOC2 summary and FedRAMP readiness note by 2026-12-24
Customer to share internal SLA acceptance matrix and minimal uptime target by 2026-12-28
Priya and Jill to coordinate a 2-hour preflight runbook + test schedule for pilot week of 2027-01-04
action_items: Alex Chen: Send security pack (SOC2 attestation, DPA summary, KMS options) - due 2026-12-24
Marta López: Share SLA acceptance spreadsheet and escrow requirements - due 2026-12-28
Priya Nair & Jill Tanner: Draft integration preflight plan and test cases (network egress, SSO, KMS) - due 2027-01-03
summary: Kickoff to align commercial acceptance, security checklist, and a technical preflight for a pilot integration. Main blockers: KMS/SSE encryption expectations, SSO/SAML alignment, and a firm SLA uptime threshold for Reserved capacity. Agreed next steps include sending security artifacts and scheduling a 2-hour technical preflight in early Jan.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta López (BlueMarsh Head of IT), Devon Price (Procurement), Samir Kapoor (Security), Jill Tanner (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, uh thanks for making time right before the holidays. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya, our sales engineer. Quick goal for today, align on governance asks and a technical preflight so your legal and platform teams can sign off for the pilot.

[01:07] Devon Price: Thanks Alex, yeah we only have, I think, 45 minutes, so we'll try to be crisp. From procurement side the main questions are: license path, SLA language, and any exceptions in the DPA/MSA. We've seen some redlines before so we want to flag them early.

[02:43] Marta López: And on the IT side we care about network egress, where the keys live, and that the offering supports VPC peering or dedicated private link. We also need to make sure that the logging/audit feed meets our retention policy, which is seven years in our case, I know it's higher than some vendors.

[03:50] Priya Nair: Totally. I'll run through the technical estate at a high level and where Redwood's options map: hosted API for fast PoC, dedicated pools for reserved throughput, and our private deployment option for bring-your-own VPC or on-prem. For the pilot you mentioned wanting isolated data, so dedicated or private are the usual choices.

[05:12] Samir Kapoor: Wait, can you say dedicated again? We need to verify what 'dedicated' means — is it single-tenant GPUs in our VPC or multi-tenant with logical isolation? That difference is important for compliance.

[05:30] Priya Nair: Good question. Our Dedicated product is a reserved GPU pool that's tenant-isolated within Redwood's hosting — so it's single-tenant compute but in Redwood-managed network. Private deployment is where the control plane is hosted but data plane can be in a customer VPC or on-prem. Some of the wording in our MSA has caused confusion so we'll point to the spec in the security pack.

[07:05] Jill Tanner: For us, private deployment is preferred, but only if we can bring our own KMS. We can't have keys exported out. Do you support external KMS/HSM, and can keys be rotated by our side?

[07:42] Alex Chen: Yes, we support BYOK patterns; Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers and HSMs. There's an option for customer-managed key pairs and rotate-in-place. We'll include the KMS integration matrix in the pack.

[08:55] Devon Price: On the legal front, our counsel flagged two DPA items — data deletion confirmation and subprocessor list. We need explicit commitments and an SLA for data purging after contract termination.

[09:30] Alex Chen: Understood. Our DPA includes data retention windows and delete confirmations, but we can add stronger language for the pilot if needed — e.g., a 30-day deletion confirmation with attestations. I will highlight where that exists now and propose wording.

[10:46] Marta López: Also, audit logs. We need to ensure we get immutable logs with timestamping, and an export path for our SIEM. Can Redwood stream logs directly into our Splunk/ELK endpoint?

[11:20] Priya Nair: Yes, we support log forwarding via syslog and secured S3 export. There are regional constraints but we can add a Splunk HEC endpoint option. We'll include example configs in the runbook.

[12:55] Samir Kapoor: Another thing — incident response. Our security team wants a 2-hour response window for Sev1 incidents and a post-incident report within 72 hours. Do your SLAs include those windows or are they negotiable?

[13:20] Alex Chen: Our standard SLA varies by plan. For Dedicated customers we aim for a 1-hour page to on-call and 4-hour severity response in prod. But we do have enterprise SLA packs where we can tighten responder windows and include post-mortem commitments. We can surface that in the commercial terms.

[14:55] Devon Price: That probably needs exec sign off, but for procurement we need a baseline: uptime target, incident SLA, and remedies. We prefer to see financial credits for missed uptime.

[16:10] Priya Nair: Right, and for pilot acceptance we usually agree on functional SLAs (latency percentiles, throughput) plus availability. For latency we can commit to p50/p95 figures on the dedicated pool with a canary test. We'll propose measurable metrics.

[17:45] Jill Tanner: On the technical side, we want to run a week-long preflight: synthetic load, KV-cache warmup, and a simulated failover. Can you support a short run where we push 10k requests/day? Also need to validate prefix caching and tokenization consistency.

[18:30] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll propose a 2-hour preflight engineering session during the first week of January, followed by a 7-day pilot. The preflight will include network checks, auth (SAML SSO flow), KMS key import, and sample inference loads to validate latency and cache behavior.

[19:50] Marta López: About SSO, our org uses Azure AD with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. Do you have a template for the SAML consumer metadata and SCIM mapping?

[20:10] Alex Chen: Yes, we have SAML and SCIM templates. We'll attach them. Note: sometimes our metadata exporter labels things a little differently; apologies if that causes mapping chores.

[21:33] Samir Kapoor: I also want to flag data residency — a few of our customers in EU expect EU-only processing and logs. Does Redwood have region locking for logs and model inference?

[22:05] Priya Nair: We have region pinning for compute and storage on Private and Dedicated. Hosted API may cross regions for redundancy unless you opt into region-restricted routes. We'll document region-residency guarantees for the pilot.

[23:40] Devon Price: Okay on pricing, procurement needs to know reserved capacity commitment and overage rates. We're likely leaning towards a 6-month pilot with an option to convert to an annual commit. What pricing cues do you need?

[24:20] Alex Chen: We'll need expected QPS, token counts per request, and retention of KV caches. If you can provide a sample traffic profile (requests per minute, average tokens in/out), we can give a cost estimate and show per-request economics comparing hosted vs dedicated.

[25:50] Jill Tanner: We also plan to test model quantization variants. Will that affect SLA or performance guarantees?

[26:10] Priya Nair: Model variants can affect throughput and latency. We run benchmarks per model/quantization profile. For SLA we specify performance bounds for the chosen model profile during the pilot. If you switch profiles mid-pilot, we'd re-benchmark.

[27:40] Marta López: Back to legal — any unusual clauses in MSA we should be aware of? Marked items like IP indemnity, jurisdiction, and export controls?

[28:00] Alex Chen: Standard MSA with mutual indemnities and export control compliance. For certain customers we accept carve-outs on jurisdiction and add UK jurisdiction options. If BlueMarsh needs specific escrow or audit rights, we can take those to legal as redlines.

[29:25] Devon Price: We will need a standard DPA plus an addendum for the payment data flow; financial data is high sensitivity, so we may request higher encryption-at-rest standards and restricted subprocessor approval.

[30:05] Samir Kapoor: Subprocessors — will you be listing cloud infra providers and any third-party telemetry vendors? We need the names up front to check for conflicts.

[30:38] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll provide the current subprocessors list — typically cloud infra, CDN, and telemetry. Note that subprocessors can change quarterly; we include a notification window in the DPA.

[31:45] Priya Nair: One small note on technical naming: sometimes our transcripts show 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' in docs — that was a small funny one in internal docs, but we will be clear in the runbook.

[32:10] Jill Tanner: Ha, 'KV cash' — noted. On the runbook, can you include an SRE contact and escalation path? We want to ensure on-call handoff during the preflight.

[32:35] Priya Nair: We'll include SRE contacts and an escalation ladder (pager, phone, email). For pilot, primary will be our SE (me) and secondary is on-call SRE. We'll mark on-call windows aligned to your test times.

[33:50] Marta López: Are there any compliance certifications in progress that we should expect next quarter? FedRAMP, ISO expansions?

[34:20] Alex Chen: We're SOC 2 Type II today, and we have a FedRAMP readiness plan — not full authorization yet but we can share the roadmap and current evidence. We're also exploring ISO 27001 expansion early next year.

[35:45] Samir Kapoor: On KMS: we want to ensure keys never leave our region and rotations are customer-initiated. Does Redwood require any key escrow for disaster recovery?

[36:05] Alex Chen: No mandatory escrow; we can operate with customer-managed keys where the key material is never exported. There are optional escrow models for some enterprise DR setups but only with explicit agreement.

[37:20] Devon Price: Great. For procurement's checklist, I need the MSA with any pilot-specific addendum, the DPA, SOC2 report, subprocessors list, and a proposed SLA redline. Can you deliver those by Friday?

[37:45] Alex Chen: Yes, I can get a security pack and redline suggestions to you by 2026-12-24. Will that work?

[38:05] Devon Price: That works. If you'll include a redline that shows proposed tightened incident windows and deletion attestations, that'll speed things up.

[39:20] Priya Nair: For the preflight schedule, Jill and I will set up a 2-hour session for network and SSO checks plus KMS key import on week of 2027-01-04. I'll follow up with a Doodle.

[40:10] Marta López: We should also do a short legal touchpoint; maybe a 30-minute sync with counsel to walk through the proposed DPA addendum. Devon can coordinate.

[41:05] Devon Price: Yup, I'll set that up after we get materials. One more procurement item: escrow for source? Not needed for this pilot but call it out if your MSA has IP escrow triggers.

[41:30] Alex Chen: Not in standard MSA; we'll note any escrow obligations that arise for special projects or long-term contracts.

[42:50] Jill Tanner: For the technical acceptance criteria — latency p95 under X ms (we'll email exact number), no data leaving EU region for EU tests, and successful SAML login and key import — are those acceptable?

[43:18] Priya Nair: Yes, that aligns with our pilot acceptance flow. We'll map those into test cases.

[44:05] Marta López: Ok let's recap then.

[44:20] Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, DPA, subprocessors, KMS matrix) by 12/24. Customer to share SLA acceptance matrix and any specific retention/jurisdiction requirements by 12/28. Priya and Jill to schedule and run a 2-hour preflight during week of 1/4 and follow with a 7-day pilot. Procurement will review proposed SLA redlines and set legal sync.

[45:10] Devon Price: Sounds good. Any blockers in principle?

[45:25] Samir Kapoor: My only outstanding is to review the SOC artifacts, but that won't block the pilot; it's more of a gating item for production.

[46:00] Alex Chen: Great. Thanks everyone — happy holidays, we'll follow up with the docs and the calendar invites.

[46:30] Marta López: Thanks, bye.

[46:40] (call ends)
